clue.text: Study occupied by a senior clergyman

indicators.note: a room occupied by someone has that person inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a den is a private study or workroom
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric's study has been taken over by a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is the head of a cathedral chapter, a senior rank in the clergy.

clue.text: Two letters for radio presenter

blocks.note: the letters D and J, each spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Someone who hosts a radio show is known by a pair of initials.
explanation.walkthrough: A DJ is a disc jockey; spelling the two initials out as words gives the informal name.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay is a disc jockey, someone who plays records and chats on air.

clue.text: Valued a piano, much admired

blocks.note: taken as written
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
something much admired is praised

explanation.surface: An auction house put a figure on a much-loved piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something, so appraised means valued in that sense.

clue.text: Director in golf club longing to acquire the lot

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: a wood is a type of golf club
a yen is a longing or craving
the lot means everything, all

explanation.surface: A film director at a golf club wants to grab everything going.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen is the American film director of Annie Hall and Manhattan.

clue.text: Several books in one vehicle

blocks.note: first meaning: a volume collecting several works
second meaning: an old name for a bus

explanation.surface: Several books being carried together in one vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition collects several works in one volume, and an omnibus is also the full name of a bus.

clue.text: Reach an agreement with party over a vintage port?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another is written above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a do is a party
taken as written
Deal in Kent is an old port, attached to the medieval Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: Sealing a deal at a party over a glass of vintage port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage port' looks like the fortified wine; it is an old harbour town, Deal on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a deal is the idiom for coming to terms or striking a bargain.

clue.text: A burden shouldered by the directors in general

blocks.note: taken as written
a cross is a burden to bear
the directors of a company form the board

explanation.surface: Company directors carrying a heavy load on their shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board is an idiom for applying to everyone or everything, i.e. universally.

clue.text: Short row about winning flower

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter is cut
about means around, so the shortened word wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a row is a line
a team that is winning is up

explanation.surface: A brief argument over a prize-winning bloom at a flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel in the surface but is used as a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Gets gen distributed about small savings

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone gathers information spread about modest savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums of money put aside for the future, so they are savings.

clue.text: Parliamentary proposal an oily Tory made, ludicrously

indicators.note: done ludicrously means put together absurdly, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A slippery Conservative MP put forward an absurd motion.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; the parliamentary sense of 'Tory' is a decoy for the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An early day motion is a House of Commons motion tabled by MPs, usually to air a cause rather than be debated.

clue.text: Interpret former patent

blocks.note: ex means former
patent in the sense of obvious, plain

explanation.surface: Someone reads the meaning of an expired patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like the noun for an invention licence; here it is the adjective meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to make its meaning clear, which is one sense of interpreting it.

clue.text: Appropriate, a truss (very large)

blocks.note: taken as written
a truss is a supporting frame, a prop
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Seemingly asking whether an oversized surgical truss is suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos describes something fitting or opportune, the same sense as appropriate.

clue.text: A bishop put in a new villa close to shrine - that's handy

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters take a fresh order
put in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

blocks.note: the article a, taken as written
letters to rearrange
A as written plus B, the chess abbreviation for bishop
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bishop lodged in a new villa near a shrine finds it convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the capital A and the lower-case a are used, one with the bishop and one at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available is at hand and ready for use, which is what handy means.

clue.text: Suspect definition

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to detect without clear evidence
second meaning: a meaning a word carries

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a crime-novel pairing; one is a verb, the other a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense trouble is to suspect it, and a sense of a word is one of its listed meanings.

clue.text: Really funny TV channel - cracking

blocks.note: old British slang for a television channel, as in 'turn over to the other side'
cracking means splitting open

explanation.surface: Praise for a hilarious, cracking show on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as British praise meaning excellent; it is used literally as breaking apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-splitting describes something so hilarious it makes one laugh until it hurts.

clue.text: Start school

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to set something up
second meaning: a noun, an educational body

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like starting at school; one word is a verb, the other a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute is to set up or begin something, and an institute is a college or place of learning.

clue.text: Greek hero you'd assess, mistakenly, as forgotten

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so those letters are removed
done mistakenly means put together wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A judgement on a Greek hero that would be wrong if he were forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey, King of Ithaca and a leader at Troy.

clue.text: Fly lengthy stages, with old man at the front

indicators.note: being at the front means coming first, so that piece leads the answer

blocks.note: old man is informal for father
lengthy means long
legs are stages of a journey

explanation.surface: An old man leads the way on a long journey by air in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb about travel, but it is the noun for the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The daddy-long-legs is the crane fly, a long-legged insect.

clue.text: What supervisor did about bladed hand tool

blocks.note: about in the sense of concerning, as in fussing over
a saw is a bladed tool used by hand

explanation.surface: A workshop foreman deals with a matter involving a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees work, so what one did is the past tense, oversaw.

clue.text: Jazz musician, proficient guy

blocks.note: proficient means good at something
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A jazz player described as a skilled fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny Goodman was the American clarinettist and bandleader known as the King of Swing.

clue.text: Remained sober, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: staid means sober and serious

explanation.surface: Someone kept off the drink, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' suggests not drinking; here it means serious and sedate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed is the past tense of stay, meaning continued in place, as remained does.

clue.text: Sudden round of applause in Oval, inappropriate after Surrey's start

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only
inappropriate means not in the proper arrangement, so the letters are reordered
one piece placed after another follows it in the answer

blocks.note: the opening letter of the county name
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Applause at the Oval feels out of place once Surrey come out to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is Surrey's county cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, and by extension a sudden burst of cheering or applause.

clue.text: Ring up about island shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Phoning about a bush on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blooms.

clue.text: Notices plastered across front of office opening in Milton Keynes?

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order
the front of a word is its first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
first letter of the word
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Notices stuck up across the front of a new office in the town of Milton Keynes.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes reads as the English new town, but the name splits: Milton supplies a letter and Keynes is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist, so he is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Cakes - girl's got her sixth in her mouth!

indicators.note: the mouth is the opening, so that letter is placed at the front

blocks.note: the sixth letter of the girl's name, Claire
the girl's name Claire's, minus the letter moved to the front

explanation.surface: A girl stuffs her mouth with cakes, her sixth one.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is Claire; her sixth letter jumps to the front of Claire's to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long cream-filled choux pastry cakes topped with chocolate.

clue.text: One associated with Queen, happy to bring in copper

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: merry means happy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A royal attendant, cheerful to welcome a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the monarch; it is the rock band, whose singer was Freddie Mercury.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of the band Queen.

clue.text: Further snake shows renewed energy

blocks.note: a further one is a second one
to snake is to wind, as a path does

explanation.surface: Another snake appears with fresh vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a fresh burst of stamina after tiredness has set in.

clue.text: Guide young man round far side of stage

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other
the far side of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

blocks.note: a lad is a young man
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Showing a young man round to the back of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone is to show them the way, which is to guide them.
